headline: Maine reopens eviction-prevention program with $11 million in aid
dek: Eligible renters who are behind on payments can seek help with past-due rent and up to 12 months of future assistance, but funding is limited.
body: Maine reopened applications Monday for a statewide eviction-prevention program funded with $11 million from the state budget. MaineHousing says the program is intended for renters who are behind on rent and at risk of losing their homes.

Households may qualify if their income is no more than 60% of the area median income and their rent meets program limits. Assistance can cover rent owed to a current landlord and, after the overdue balance is addressed, as much as 12 months of additional rental support, with total help capped at $9,600 per household.

Applications will be prioritized for eligible households that have received a court summons related to eviction, followed by those with an eviction notice for nonpayment and applicants who spend more than 30% of their income on rent. Complete applications are then reviewed in the order they are received, and MaineHousing warns that available funds may run out.

MaineHousing is administering the program with Project Home, which handles application review and communication with tenants and landlords. Maine Public reported that a prior pilot served about 1,300 households and that the new program is expected to draw heavy demand; applications are available through MaineHousing online, by phone or with paper assistance from Project Home.
author: NorthEast News Desk
